source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; Oscar Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extracts harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions, ablates the selected direction across layers and positions, and adds it at its source layer. It also tests an equivalent weight edit and examines an adversarial suffix's effect on the direction.
record.gate_note: The direction-selection scores in Table 5 are used to select a direction, not reported outcomes of the claim, so they are not rows. Cited results from other work are not rows. The paper also reports separate safety scores in Figure 1; those are recorded alongside refusal scores. The text states that weight orthogonalization is equivalent to directional ablation. The main figures do not provide extractable numerical values in the text.
record.test_reason: This is the original source for the claim. It extracts harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions in 13 chat models. It ablates the direction (Fig 1) and adds it (Fig 3), implements ablation as a weight edit evaluated on HarmBench (Table 2) and capability benchmarks (Tables 3, 8, 9), and analyses one adversarial suffix (Fig 5) and base-model expression (Fig 24). Because it is the original source, no verdict labels are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state the direction is already present in base models and repurposed during safety fine-tuning (§J). They state that orthogonalization consistently lowers TruthfulQA, and that Qwen 7B and Yi 34B show significant drops on some other benchmarks. They frame the work as an existence proof using heuristic direction extraction.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means vectors, selects one candidate per model, ablates the unit direction across all residual-stream layers and positions, and adds the unnormalized vector at its selected layer. The weight orthogonalization edit is described as equivalent to the ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: The weight-edit attack success rate depends on system prompt and model family: Llama-2 results change substantially with system prompts, while Qwen results remain similar. Llama-2 7B's ASR across 12 prompts has mean 30.0% and standard deviation 23.3%; Qwen 7B's has mean 76.7% and standard deviation 5.9%.
record.problems: Main refusal/addition figures provide no numeric values in the text, only plots and qualitative descriptions. Refusal is scored by substring matching, and harmfulness by a classifier; the authors note limitations of these measures. Adversarial-suffix analysis is limited to one model and one suffix. The paper reports TruthfulQA drops for orthogonalized models and statistically significant drops on some other benchmark/model combinations; the broader coherence metrics and exceptions are not fully represented in the kept rows.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted Figure 3 safety-related measures if any beyond its refusal score; omitted the rest of Table 8 and Table 9 CE-loss results, Table 10 fine-tuning comparison, and additional general-capability benchmark rows. Table 8 reports MMLU, TinyHellaSwag, ARC, WinoGrande, GSM8K and TruthfulQA for 13 models; Table 9 reports CE loss across three datasets and interventions. The text says most non-TruthfulQA capability changes are small, with significant exceptions for Qwen 7B and Yi 34B. Also omitted other Table 2 comparator methods and Table 7/§F.2 system-prompt conditions beyond the with/without-prompt entries in Table 2.

untested.parts: Training against ablation for robustness is not tested. The jailbreak analysis covers one suffix on one model (Qwen 1.8B).
Cross-language transfer and transfer across other model variants are not tested. The base-model result shows the direction is expressed (cosine similarity), not that it is causal in base models.
Not tested. The authors note the direction may encode 'harm' rather than refusal.

missing.what: Negative activation addition (subtracting the vector) bypasses refusal about as well as ablation but raises CE loss more (Fig 23, Table 9). Rows_left_out covers Table 9 but not the Fig 23 refusal result.

record.verdict_notes: The study is the original source for all versions, so verdict labels are withheld. The reader's 'partial' states on the Figure 1 rows are not supported by the text and are changed to cannot_determine, except the Llama-3 8B rows, which Table 10 quantifies.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests selected directions in 13 open-source chat models, not all safety-trained models. Addition is at the selected source layer, not all layers; it does not test other ways of selecting directions.
Weight orthogonalization is evaluated on the reported models and HarmBench conditions; the paper does not test every released model or deployment setting.
It studies one adversarial suffix on Qwen 1.8B Chat. It does not train against ablation or test whether such training improves robustness.
The paper measures refusal and harmfulness separately but does not test whether harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from the refusal decision.
It compares expression of chat-derived directions in four corresponding base models; it does not test cross-language transfer or transfer across other model variants.

source_check.notes: The record's controls=y is generous. The text has no random-direction control for ablation or addition. Its only explicit control is the random suffix in §5, plus no-intervention and DR baselines and the kl_score filter. Table 10 gives stated Llama-3 8B ablation numbers (0.95->0.01 refusal; 0.97->0.15 safety); check that the Llama-3 8B row uses them rather than 'figure only'. The authors_conclusion says Qwen 7B and Yi 34B show 'significant drops'. The text only says some of their metrics fall outside 99% CIs (e.g. Qwen 7B GSM8K 48.1->41.8), and some move up.

statements.problem: Gives no number or claim about this study in the visible text.

statements.correction: Optional addition from §F.2: across 12 system prompts, ASR for orthogonalized Llama-2 7B has mean 30.0%, SD 23.3%; for Qwen 7B, mean 76.7%, SD 5.9%.

§J: base models show high cosine with the chat-derived direction on harmful prompts and low cosine on harmless ones, as chat models do (Qwen 1.8B, Gemma 7B, Qwen 14B, Llama-3 8B; figure only). The authors conclude the representation 'exists already in the base model' and is repurposed during safety fine-tuning. No causal test is run in base models.
statements.problem: Wording suggests the original says its result shows 'expression, not causation'. That caveat comes from the catalog record, not from the paper.

statements.correction: The original's base evidence is correlational: chat-direction cosine in base activations, figure only. The authors infer the direction 'is repurposed for refusal during safety fine-tuning'. The point that this is not causal is the catalog's.
